theory.title: Transmitir lo que otras personas dicen y preguntan
theory.explanation: El estilo indirecto permite contar a otra persona lo que alguien dijo o preguntó sin repetir sus palabras exactas. Cuando el verbo introductor está en pasado (said, told, asked), suele producirse un cambio de tiempo verbal: present simple → past simple, present continuous → past continuous, past simple → past perfect, will → would y can → could. Utiliza say para introducir palabras y tell + persona para indicar a quién se las dijeron. En preguntas indirectas conserva el orden afirmativo y utiliza if/whether en preguntas de sí o no. También pueden cambiar expresiones de tiempo y lugar según el momento desde el que hablas.
theory.tip: No uses el orden de pregunta directa: “Where do you live?” → He asked where I lived. Recuerda tell + persona, pero say + palabras.

patterns.label: Estilo indirecto: afirmaciones
patterns.pattern: Para transmitir lo que alguien dijo, utiliza say/tell + (that) + oración. Si el verbo introductor está en pasado, normalmente retrocede un tiempo: present simple → past simple; present perfect → past perfect; will → would.
examples:
He said (that) he was tired.
→ Él dijo que estaba cansado.

patterns.label: Say y tell: decir y contar
patterns.pattern: Say se centra en las palabras y normalmente no lleva persona directamente después; tell necesita un complemento de persona: tell me, tell us, tell Anna.
examples:
He said he was busy.
→ Ella me dijo que necesitaba ayuda.

patterns.label: Presente pasa a pasado
patterns.pattern: En estilo indirecto, present simple suele cambiar a past simple y present continuous a past continuous cuando el verbo introductor está en pasado.
examples:
“I work here.” → She said she worked there.
→ Él dijo que estaba ocupado.

patterns.label: Pasado pasa a past perfect
patterns.pattern: Past simple suele cambiar a past perfect para dejar claro que la acción ocurrió antes de la conversación.
examples:
“I lost my keys.” → He said he had lost his keys.
→ Él me dijo que estaba ocupado.

patterns.label: Will pasa a would
patterns.pattern: Will suele cambiar a would al transmitir una promesa, predicción o decisión futura desde un punto de vista pasado.
examples:
“I'll call you.” → She said she would call me.
→ «Trabajo aquí». → Ella dijo que trabajaba allí.

patterns.label: Can/may pasan a could/might
patterns.pattern: Can suele cambiar a could y may a might en estilo indirecto cuando el verbo introductor está en pasado.
examples:
“I can help.” → He said he could help.
→ «Perdí las llaves». → Él dijo que había perdido las llaves.

patterns.label: Estilo indirecto: preguntas informativas
patterns.pattern: En preguntas indirectas no hay inversión sujeto-verbo ni do/does/did. Utiliza orden afirmativo después de la palabra interrogativa o if/whether.
examples:
“Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.
→ «Te llamaré». → Ella dijo que me llamaría.

patterns.label: Preguntas de sí/no
patterns.pattern: Para transmitir preguntas de sí/no, utiliza ask + if/whether + sujeto + verbo. No mantengas el orden de pregunta directa.
examples:
“Are you ready?” → He asked if I was ready.
→ «Puedo ayudar». → Él dijo que podía ayudar.

patterns.label: Cambios de tiempo y lugar
patterns.pattern: Según el contexto, today puede pasar a that day, tomorrow a the next day, here a there y now a then.
examples:
“I'll come tomorrow.” → She said she would come the next day.
→ «¿Dónde vives?». → Ella preguntó dónde vivía.

patterns.label: Sin retroceso verbal si sigue siendo cierto
patterns.pattern: No siempre es obligatorio cambiar el tiempo si la información sigue siendo cierta o el contexto no requiere retroceso.
examples:
The teacher said that water boils at 100°C.
→ «¿Estás listo?». → Él preguntó si estaba listo.

phrases.spanish: Dijo que se encontraba mucho mejor.

phrases.english: He told me that the train was delayed.
phrases.spanish: Me dijo que el tren llevaba retraso.

phrases.english: Marta explained that she had missed the bus.
phrases.spanish: Marta explicó que había perdido el autobús.

phrases.english: They promised they would keep in touch.
I was told that the meeting had been cancelled.
phrases.spanish: Me dijeron que la reunión se había cancelado.

phrases.english: He asked me where I had bought the jacket.
phrases.spanish: Me preguntó dónde había comprado la chaqueta.

phrases.english: She wanted to know if I could help.
According to Sam, the shop was closing early.
phrases.spanish: Según Sam, la tienda cerraba pronto.

phrases.english: He admitted that he had forgotten the message.
phrases.spanish: Admitió que había olvidado el mensaje.

phrases.english: She reminded us to bring our tickets.
phrases.spanish: Nos recordó que lleváramos las entradas.

Tom said he had seen the film.
Ana said she would phone later.
He said he could speak French.
He asked if I was free.
They said they would return the following day.

reading.english: Read a short account of a family conversation and identify how the speaker reports different statements and questions.
reading.spanish: Lee un relato breve de una conversación familiar e identifica cómo se transmiten distintas afirmaciones y preguntas.

writing.english: Write a short message reporting three things a friend told you, including one question and one promise.
writing.spanish: Escribe un mensaje breve contando tres cosas que te dijo un amigo, incluida una pregunta y una promesa.

speaking.english: Retell a conversation you had recently. Explain what the other person said, asked or promised.
speaking.spanish: Cuenta una conversación reciente. Explica qué dijo, preguntó o prometió la otra persona.

listening.english: Listen for reported statements, reported questions and changes in time expressions.
listening.spanish: Escucha afirmaciones y preguntas en estilo indirecto y cambios en expresiones temporales.

examples.english: Lucy said she had moved the meeting because she would be travelling the next day.
examples.spanish: Lucy dijo que había cambiado la reunión porque viajaría al día siguiente.
examples.note: Reported statement with past perfect and would.

communication.english: He told me that… / She asked whether…
communication.spanish: Me dijo que… / Me preguntó si…
communication.note: Resume las ideas principales sin repetir literalmente toda la conversación.

items.answer: That Grandpa had shared fascinating memories

content.passage: When Olivia visited her grandfather last weekend, he told her several stories about his childhood. He said that he had grown up in a small village and that children had spent most of their time outdoors. He explained that there had been no computers at home, so they had listened to the radio in the evenings. Olivia asked whether he had enjoyed school. He replied that he had loved science but had found mathematics difficult. He also told her that his older sister had taught him to repair bicycles. Olivia asked how he had learned to cook, and he said that his mother had shown him simple recipes. Before Olivia left, her grandfather reminded her to write down the family stories because he thought they were worth keeping. He promised that he would tell her more about their relatives next time. On the way home, Olivia messaged her brother and said that Grandpa had shared some fascinating memories. Her brother replied that he wanted to visit soon too.

items.prompt: Report something interesting a family member told you recently.
items.modelAnswer: My grandfather told me that he had travelled around Europe when he was young. He said he had visited several countries and had met many interesting people.

items.prompt: Describe a conversation in which someone gave you useful advice.
items.modelAnswer: A friend told me that I should take more breaks. She explained that working for hours without resting made it harder to concentrate.

items.prompt: Retell a time when someone asked you for help.
items.modelAnswer: My neighbour asked me whether I could look after her plants while she was away. I said I would be happy to help.

items.prompt: Explain how you would report a rumour responsibly.
items.modelAnswer: I would say who had shared the information and make it clear that I did not know whether it was true. I would avoid presenting it as a fact.

items.prompt: Tell a short story using at least three reported statements.
items.modelAnswer: My cousin said she had found a new job. She told me that the team was friendly and promised she would send me the details.

items.prompt: Describe a question someone asked you and how you reported it later.
items.modelAnswer: A colleague asked me if I was free on Friday. Later, I told my manager that he wanted to arrange a meeting.

items.prompt: Report a promise that someone made to you.
items.modelAnswer: My friend promised that he would help me move house. He said he could bring his car and told me to contact him the day before.

items.prompt: Explain the difference between say and tell with examples.
items.modelAnswer: We use say to report words, as in “She said she was tired”. We use tell with a person, as in “She told me she was tired”.

items.prompt: Describe a story you heard from an older person.
items.modelAnswer: My aunt told me that she had lived abroad for two years. She explained that she had learned the language by speaking to local people.

items.prompt: Summarise a conversation without repeating every word.
items.modelAnswer: I would identify the main points, use said, told and asked, and change the verb tenses where necessary. I would also change time expressions if the context required it.

content.audioTranscript: Nora: Did you speak to Ben after the meeting? Alex: Yes. He said he had enjoyed the discussion. Nora: What did he think about the new project? Alex: He told me that the idea was practical, but he asked whether we had enough time. Nora: Did you answer him? Alex: I said that we were checking the schedule. He also mentioned that he could help with the research. Nora: That's useful. Did he say when he was available? Alex: He said he would be free the following week. Nora: And what did the manager say? Alex: She explained that the deadline had changed and reminded everyone to send their notes by Friday. Nora: I see. Did she promise to confirm the details? Alex: Yes, she said she would email us the next day.
